priorityReason: It is what an incident investigation reads, and what a disputed gate scan is checked against.

goal.outcome: an incident can be investigated, and a disputed gate scan can be checked

Visits were listed with the visitor, who they came to see, the time in, the time out, and whether the departure was confirmed or closed unconfirmed.
Staff arrivals and departures were read from the attendance record rather than held a second time here.
Open visits and outstanding passes were shown as a list of their own, so the desk could chase them.
The log was read in an incident investigation, and against the attendance record where a gate scan was disputed.
Reading it required a permission the Super Admin granted, because it holds the movements of named people.

businessRules.rule: The log is opened for a chosen date, gate and branch.
Visits are listed with the visitor, who they came to see, the time in, the time out, and whether the departure was confirmed or closed unconfirmed.

Staff arrivals and departures are read from the attendance record rather than held a second time here. A member of staff's scan at the gate is the attendance record and not a second feature on top of it.
Open visits and outstanding passes are shown as a list of their own, so that the desk can chase them.
Reading the log is a permission the Super Admin grants, because it holds the movements of named people. Nobody holds it by default.
The log is read in any incident investigation, and against the attendance record where a gate scan is disputed.
Students are not in the log at all. A student shows their card so the guard can see they belong to the school, the guard admits them, and nothing enters the system.
The log is read-only. Nothing is corrected here; a wrong visit is corrected where it was recorded and a wrong attendance mark through the attendance correction route.
A branch-scoped reader sees only their own branch's log, since branches are sealed.
Every reading of the log is itself recorded, since it holds the movements of named people.
The log cannot answer which students are on campus, and does not claim to. Attendance records who was marked present that morning, not who is in the building now.

departures.aspect: No second copy of staff movements
departures.requirement: Staff arrivals and departures are read from the attendance record. The log holds no copy of them, so the two can never disagree.
Every reading is written to the audit trail, since the log holds the movements of named people.
The log states plainly that it does not cover students, rather than presenting an incomplete answer to who is on campus.
A visitor record holds personal data belonging to somebody not otherwise connected to the school, and no retention period is set for it.

openQuestions.question: A visitor record holds a name, a contact number and the purpose of a visit — personal data belonging to somebody who is not otherwise connected to the school — and no retention period is set for it.

Students are not recorded at the gate, so the school cannot say which students are on campus at any moment. Attendance records who was marked present that morning, not who is in the building now, which is what a gate log exists to answer during a fire or a lockdown.
openQuestions.assumption: Unresolved. This is the largest gap in the module.

openQuestions.question: A child leaving during the day with an adult is recorded nowhere, which is the highest-risk event at any school gate. Whether an early collection is recorded, and by whom, is undecided.
openQuestions.assumption: Unresolved, and the pickup card issued in 13.1 has no gate process to be presented to.

openQuestions.question: Nothing says what the gate should refuse. Whether a day the calendar marks closed refuses entry, whether a person's timetable bears on it, and whether any opening-hours window applies are all undefined.
openQuestions.assumption: Unresolved. The one rule stated is that a cancelled card or biometric enrolment no longer opens the gate.

openQuestions.question: Does the school have more than one gate, and is the log read per gate?
openQuestions.assumption: Modelled as filterable by gate. No feature creates a gate.

conventionsApplied.name: session-and-authentication
conventionsApplied.rule: Every use case except the login use case assumes an authenticated session. Sign out is available on every screen. An expired or invalid session returns the user to the login screen with the message "Your session has ended. Please sign in again."

conventionsApplied.name: role-based-access
conventionsApplied.rule: Access is enforced server-side on every request, not only by hiding menu items. A request for a record outside the actor's permitted scope returns a 403 and the message "You do not have permission to view this record." A use case states additions and restrictions only.

conventionsApplied.name: branch-scope
conventionsApplied.rule: Every record carries a branch ID. Users see only their own branch unless the use case states otherwise. Super Admin, School Admin and Principal may switch branch from the header.

conventionsApplied.name: list-screens
conventionsApplied.rule: Every list supports search, column sort and page-size selection. Default page size 25; default sort is most recent first. Filters are applied before printing or exporting.

conventionsApplied.name: print-and-pdf
conventionsApplied.rule: Every report and list offers Print and Download as PDF, honouring the filters currently applied. Each output carries the school name, branch, academic session, report title, filter summary, generation timestamp and the name of the user who generated it.

conventionsApplied.name: audit-trail
conventionsApplied.rule: Every create, update, deactivation, approval and reversal writes to the audit log: actor, role, timestamp, record type, record ID, before and after values, and IP address. Audit entries are never editable.

conventionsApplied.name: validation-and-messages
conventionsApplied.rule: Field-level errors appear inline beneath the field on blur and on submit. Errors that block the whole action appear as a banner at the top of the form. Successful actions show a toast. No action succeeds silently.

conventionsApplied.name: dates-times-numbers
conventionsApplied.rule: Dates display as DD-MM-YYYY; date and time as DD-MM-YYYY HH:mm in 24-hour form. Times are school-local. Phone numbers are stored in the registered mobile format.

conventionsApplied.name: language
conventionsApplied.rule: All user-visible strings come from a resource file. No hard-coded text in any screen.

conventionsApplied.name: screen-states
conventionsApplied.rule: Every list, dashboard tile and report defines four states: loading, empty, error and populated. The empty state names what is missing and links to the action that creates it.

conventionsApplied.name: notifications
conventionsApplied.rule: All outbound SMS, WhatsApp, email and push messages are sent through the Messaging module, recorded in the sent-message log with per-channel delivery status, and use a named template. Use cases reference the template; they do not embed message text.

conventionsApplied.name: default-performance-and-retention
conventionsApplied.rule: Unless a use case states otherwise: a screen loads within 2 seconds and a save completes within 2 seconds at 200 concurrent users; lists paginate above 100 rows; financial and student records are retained 7 years; audit and message logs 12 months; every screen is usable at a 360 px viewport. Fill the non-functional field only to depart from this.

conventionsApplied.name: default-trigger
conventionsApplied.rule: Unless a use case states otherwise, the trigger is: the user navigates to the screen and initiates the action. Fill the Triggers field only where a scheduled job, an event in another module, or an inbound external call also starts it.
